draft.title: Director, Office of Research Ethics
draft.position_summary: Briefly describe the primary function and purpose of the position in one or two sentences. Reporting to the Vice-President, Research, the Director provides leadership and manages the operations of the Office of Research Ethics. The Director ensures compliance with SFU’s Policy R20.01 (Ethics Review of Research Involving Human Subjects) and the Tri-Council Policy Statement: Ethical Conduct in Research Involving Humans (TCPS 2). The incumbent of the position provides interpretation of policies concerning the ethical conduct of research to faculty members, staff, and students through ethics review, educational activities and resources, and in a peer-advisory capacity. The Director acts as the primary contact for the university with external bodies including the health authorities, hospitals, ministries, and foundations; engages in internal and external liaison activities on behalf of the Research Ethics Board (REB); represents SFU on boards or committees; and liaises with aboriginal individuals and communities concerning collaborative research activities. The Director prepares an annual report of activities which the REB is required to provide Senate at its September meeting.

model.title: Director, Office of Research Ethics
model.position_summary: The Director provides strategic leadership and operational oversight for the Office of Research Ethics, ensuring that all human‑subjects research at SFU complies with Policy R20.01 and the Tri‑Council Policy Statement (TCPS‑2). The role interprets ethical policies, guides faculty, staff and students through the ethics review process, and represents the university in internal and external forums. By managing staff, reviewing applications, handling participant concerns, and maintaining accurate records and reporting, the Director safeguards ethical standards and supports the university’s research mission.

duties.statement: leadership and manage the operations of the Office of Research Ethics
how_why: ensure compliance with SFU Policy R20.01 and TCPS‑2
oversee day‑to‑day activities and supervise staff
develop and implement office procedures and policies

duties.statement: research ethics applications for completeness and policy compliance
how_why: approve minimal‑risk applications and document rationale
consult the REB Chair on greater‑than‑minimal‑risk studies
return incomplete applications to investigators for revision

duties.statement: as the primary liaison between SFU and external bodies on ethics matters
how_why: act as contact for health authorities, hospitals, ministries and foundations
represent SFU on external committees and boards such as the MSFHR Ethics Harmonization Initiative
engage with Aboriginal individuals and communities for collaborative research

duties.statement: to concerns or complaints from research participants
how_why: investigate issues, act as liaison between participants and researchers
facilitate resolution or refer matters beyond Policy R20.01 scope

duties.statement: records management, monitoring and reporting activities
how_why: ensure timeliness, accuracy and availability of reports for funding sponsors and university committees
prepare the annual REB activity report for Senate
collect and analyse data to inform policy updates and inter‑university communication

decision_making: Operational management of the Office of Research Ethics and supervision of staff
Interpretation and application of ethics policies and procedures
Referral of significant legal or financial matters to the Vice‑President, Research
problem_solving: Resolving sensitive internal ethics issues and participant complaints
Addressing complex applications that may exceed minimal risk
Coordinating responses to external inquiries and legislative requirements

relationships.supervisory: Directly supervises 2 full‑time staff members and oversees additional part‑time staff

qualifications.text: University degree (e.g., Master's) in a relevant discipline or an equivalent combination of education, training and experience
Significant experience in research ethics administration and review processes
Knowledge of SFU Policy R20.01, TCPS‑2 and related federal/provincial regulations
Demonstrated leadership and staff management abilities
Strong communication and liaison skills with internal and external stakeholders
